why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
when two lists have the same number of members they pair up IN ORDER (yathāsaṅkhya) — they pair up in order (यथासङ्ख्यम्)

why.txt: runs on from 7.1.3 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.1.44 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.1.38 (anuvṛtti)

left.txt: a substitute of more than one sound (or शित्) replaces the WHOLE — तिप् etc.: more than one sound → it replaces the WHOLE of the place

teaching_view.fin: छन्दसि विषये अङ्गस्य तस्य स्थाने तप् तनप् तन थन इत्येते आदेशाः भवन्ति

why.txt: the augment stands in the 1st case
a टित् augment goes at the BEGINNING, a कित् one at the END — it goes at the END of the place (after the last sound of the aṅga)
runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.1.38 (anuvṛtti)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

An अण् (vowels, semivowels, ह) or an उदित् (कु = the k-class) in a rule also stands for its savarṇas: उ = उवर्ण, short, long and pluta. Not when that sound is itself what the rule introduces, and not when त् follows it — then only 1.1.70. (Kaumudī: “अविधीयमानोऽण् उदिच्च सवर्णस्य संज्ञा स्यात्”)

runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”
अनङ् is ङित्: though it has several sounds it replaces only the last sound (not the whole, as 1.1.55 would have it)
the accent named in the 1st case is the result

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.1.73 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.1.73 (anuvṛtti)

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72) — → अजादौ (what BEGINS with it), as the नैलेश-वृत्तिः reads it
runs on from 7.1.74 (anuvṛtti)
runs on from 7.1.72 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
गो here means the word गो itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

as the काशिका reads it

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

the substitute chosen is the NEAREST in articulation — वृद्धि replaces a vowel → the nearest guṇa/vṛddhi sound is chosen
ऋ replaced by a / i / u comes with र् — when the vowel replaced is ऋ/ऌ → it comes with र्/ल् (अर्, आर्, अल्)
a substitute replaces only the LAST sound — the place is a whole aṅga/dhātu and the replacement is one sound → it replaces the LAST sound → अन्त्यस्य अलः

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.1 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.35 (anuvṛtti)
as the काशिका reads it

An augment (āgama) marked ṭ is joined as the first part, one marked k as the last part, of the item named in the 6th case; with a 5th case it goes on what follows. It replaces nothing, and a ṭ/k marker on a suffix or a substitute does not bring in this rule. (Kāśikā: “आदिष्टिद् भवति अन्तःकिद् भवति षष्ठीनिर्दिष्टस्य”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.35 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
as the प्रथमावृत्तिः reads it
runs on from 7.2.38 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.35 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.76 (anuvṛtti)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
ई replaces the first sound of आन after आस् — SK: “आसः परस्यानस्य ईत्स्यात् । आदेः परस्य”
runs on from 7.2.82 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: runs on from 7.2.84 (anuvṛtti)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.2.84 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
it describes another word of the rule

no.txt: names a qualification, not what follows

left.txt: a substitute replaces only the LAST sound — आ: a single sound → it replaces the LAST sound

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72) — हलि (from 7.2.85; the anuvṛtti data leaves it out): a sound group in the 7th → → हलादौ (what BEGINS with it), as the Siddhānta-kaumudī, Laghu-kaumudī read it

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

corrected by the paribhāṣā audit: Credit licensed (6.4.1 adhikāra in force), but our vṛtti renders the carried अङ्गस्य as an apposition of the suffix/sound being replaced or augmented ("…स्थाने अङ्गस्य स्थाने…"); the source construes it as the base (अङ्गात् / अङ्गस्य … उत्तरस्य), per C6.

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”
a substitute of more than one sound (or शित्) replaces the WHOLE — it replaces the WHOLE of the place

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.91 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.2.86 (anuvṛtti)
when two lists have the same number of members they pair up IN ORDER (yathāsaṅkhya) — they pair up in order (यथासङ्ख्यम्)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.2.84 (anuvṛtti)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.2.106 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

left.txt: a substitute replaces only the LAST sound — the place is a whole aṅga/dhātu and the replacement is one sound → it replaces the LAST sound → अन्त्यस्य अलः

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.109 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.2.108 (anuvṛtti)

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72)

why.txt: runs on from 7.2.114 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
a vowel with त् after it (तपर) means only that one length — only the short अ
runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
it describes another word of the rule

paribhashas.trigger: आत्: आ with त् after it (तपर)
paribhashas.effect: only the long आ, not its other lengths

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

When a rule has two lists with the same number of members, first goes with first, second with second. Unequal lists do not pair; where the commentators say the pairing is not meant, it does not apply; where nearness decides, it is 1.1.50. runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 7.2.114 (anuvṛtti)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.3.10 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 7.2.117 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.3.10 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.3.10 (anuvṛtti)
runs on from 7.3.13 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 7.2.117 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.3.10 (anuvṛtti)
runs on from 7.3.15 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)
runs on from 7.3.10 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

why.txt: runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.3.10 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.2.117 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. आतः qualifies अङ्गस्य (the heading from 6.4.1, both in the 6th) — a qualifier agreeing with the word it qualifies stands for whatever ends in it → “आकारान्तस्य अङ्गस्य”

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
a vowel with त् after it (तपर) means only that one length — only the long आ
runs on from 7.2.115 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

An augment (āgama) marked ṭ is joined as the first part, one marked k as the last part, of the item named in the 6th case; with a 5th case it goes on what follows. It replaces nothing, and a ṭ/k marker on a suffix or a substitute does not bring in this rule. (Kāśikā: “आदिष्टिद् भवति अन्तःकिद् भवति षष्ठीनिर्दिष्टस्य”)
when two lists have the same number of members they pair up IN ORDER (yathāsaṅkhya) — they pair up in order (यथासङ्ख्यम्)
runs on from 7.3.36 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

paribhashas.effect: only the long आ, not its other lengths

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.3.55 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 7.3.70 (anuvṛtti)

ओतः qualifies अङ्गस्य (the heading from 6.4.1, both in the 6th) — a qualifier agreeing with the word it qualifies stands for whatever ends in it → “ओकारान्तस्य अङ्गस्य”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

left.txt: a substitute replaces only the LAST sound — the place is a whole aṅga/dhātu and the replacement is one sound → it replaces the LAST sound → अन्त्यस्य अलः

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”
दीर्घ is taught by its own name, so it falls only on a vowel (अचः) — काशिका on 1.2.28: “ह्रस्वदीर्घप्लुताः स्वसंज्ञया शिष्यमाणा अच एव स्थाने वेदितव्याः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
it describes another word of the rule

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.3.75 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

left.txt: a substitute replaces only the LAST sound — छ्: a single sound → it replaces the LAST sound

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.3.75 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

runs on from 7.3.75 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 7.3.89 (anuvṛtti)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
ऊर्णोतेः: dhātu named in its श्तिप् form → = the dhātu ऊर्णु
runs on from 7.3.87 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.3.87 (anuvṛtti)
runs on from 7.3.89 (anuvṛtti)

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
the augment stands in the 1st case

An element marked with म् (नुम्, मुम्, श्नम्, अम्) goes right after the last vowel of what it is added to and becomes its final part. It replaces nothing: it overrides both the ‘in place of’ reading and the rule that a suffix follows. (Kāśikā: “अचां संनिविष्टानामन्त्यादचः परो मिद् भवति।”)
runs on from 7.3.87 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.3.104 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)
runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

paribhashas.effect: only the short ऋ, not its other lengths

the option word here carries the meaning itself — the saṃjñā is not needed (Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.44: “आचार्यः खल्वपि सञ्ज्ञामारभमाणो भूयिष्ठमन्यैरपि शब्दैरेतमर्थं सम्प्रत्याययति - बहुलमन्यतरस्यामुभयथा वा एकेषामिति”)

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.4.9 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
ऋतः qualifies अङ्गस्य (the heading from 6.4.1, both in the 6th) — a qualifier agreeing with the word it qualifies stands for whatever ends in it → “ऋकारान्तस्य”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
ऊहतेः: dhātu named in its श्तिप् form → = the dhātu ऊह्

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 7.4.22 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.4.22 (anuvṛtti)

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72)
runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.4.29 (anuvṛtti)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.4.32 (anuvṛtti)
अस्य qualifies अङ्गस्य (the heading from 6.4.1, both in the 6th) — a qualifier agreeing with the word it qualifies stands for whatever ends in it → “अवर्णान्तस्य”
a word in the 6th case in a rule names WHAT IS REPLACED — so we read “… स्थाने” — names the place — the thing replaced (“स्थाने”)

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.4.33 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.4.40 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.4.40 (anuvṛtti)

runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.4.40 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.4.40 (anuvṛtti)

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72)
it describes another word of the rule

The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.4.46 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
runs on from 7.4.40 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.4.40 (anuvṛtti)

runs on from 7.4.46 (anuvṛtti)
a word in the 6th case in a rule names WHAT IS REPLACED — so we read “… स्थाने” — names the place — the thing replaced (“स्थाने”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.4.49 (anuvṛtti)
सः (carried over from 7.4.49) qualifies अङ्गस्य (the heading from 6.4.1) — a qualifier agreeing with the word it qualifies stands for whatever ends in it → “सकारस्य”

a SOUND (a letter, a pratyāhāra, or the augment इट् — not a suffix or a word) in the 7th case, qualifying a 7th-case condition, stands for what BEGINS with it — so we read “…-आदि” (an exception to tadanta-vidhi, 1.1.72)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.4.50 (anuvṛtti)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

paribhashas.trigger: ईत्: ई with त् after it (तपर)
paribhashas.effect: only the long ई, not its other lengths

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. Check it is a real tapara: आत् may be the 5th case of अ (आद्गुणः), and a त् may belong to the form. (Kāśikā: “तपरो वर्णस्तत्कालस्यात्मना तुल्यकालस्य … ग्राहको भवति”)

The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

why.txt: न — the rule says “not”
runs on from 7.4.62 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
कवतेः: dhātu named in its श्तिप् form → = the dhātu कव्

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.4.58 (anuvṛtti)

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
उः qualifies अङ्गस्य (the heading from 6.4.1, both in the 6th) — a qualifier agreeing with the word it qualifies stands for whatever ends in it → “ऋवर्णान्तस्य”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
इकः (supplied by 1.1.3) qualifies अङ्गस्य (the heading from 6.4.1) — a qualifier agreeing with the word it qualifies stands for whatever ends in it → “अङ्गस्य”
runs on from 7.4.58 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
runs on from 7.4.58 (anuvṛtti)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
as the प्रथमावृत्तिः reads it
runs on from 7.4.82 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. paribhashas.effect: only the short अ, not its other lengths

why.txt: A vowel with त् after it stands only for vowels of its own length: अत् = short अ, आत् = long आ, एत्/ओत् = two-mora ए/ओ, not pluta. q: on which stem (aṅga) does it operate?

why.txt: runs on from 6.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

What a suffix was introduced after — a dhātu or prātipadika, with any vikaraṇa or augment added to it — is the aṅga of that suffix. The अङ्गस्य heading (6.4.1) runs to the end of book 7; it names the base, not necessarily the part that changes. (Kāśikā: “यस्मात् प्रत्ययो विधीयते … प्रत्यये परतोऽङ्गसंज्ञं भवति।”)
runs on from 7.4.58 (anuvṛtti)
runs on from 7.4.1 (anuvṛtti)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
runs on from 7.4.93 (anuvṛtti)
it describes another word of the rule

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)
